mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the prior 3 months compresses discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.25 percentage points over the prior 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 5.5% in a 3-month window, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 5.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in residential housing starts (HOUST) and real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) indicates weakening consumer demand, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced corporate revenue growth.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative returns when the correlation between the two series drops below 0.7 in a 6-month window.

mechanism_narrative: In the late-cycle expansion regime, a sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 110.0 for 3 consecutive months signals robust manufacturing activity that supports corporate profit growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO exceeds 110.0 in the late-cycle expansion regime.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year change in CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0%, it indicates accelerating inflation that prompts the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL rises above 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 2.0% and a year-over-year CPIAUCSL increase exceeding 3.0% signals aggressive monetary tightening amid inflation, compressing equity valuations and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of FEDFUNDS > 2.0% and CPIAUCSL > 3.0% fails to predict negative returns when the correlation between the two series drops below 0.8 in a 6-month window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption (RSAFS) over the prior 6 months indicates strong consumer spending that supports corporate revenue growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when RSAFS increases by at least 0.5% over 6 months.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly change in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) falls below 50,000 persons, it indicates slowing job growth that reduces household income and consumer spending, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS change falls below 50,000 persons.
